habitat: Lowland mature forests; forest edge; secondary growth; and wooded areas
story: In the diverse world of birds, the Black Hornbill (Anthracoceros malayanus) stands out. This species, part of the Bucerotidae family, is a resident of Lowland mature forests; forest edge; secondary growth; and wooded areas. Its IUCN Red List status is Vulnerable (VU), which serves as a call to action for habitat preservation. The Black Hornbill is more than just a bird; it is a symbol of the rich biodiversity that we must protect. Through this poster, we hope to foster a greater understanding and appreciation for the Black Hornbill and its role in the ecosystem.
Every poster is crafted to inspire curiosity about our planet's incredible biodiversity.
